name: Medial meniscus — body
description: Middle third of the medial meniscus, its rim fixed to the deep MCL so there is no normal gap to the capsule. A sharp low-signal triangle on coronal images and the bow tie on peripheral sagittal images; it covers about half the medial plateau.

normal_values.bow_tie_count_on_sagittal: 2 or more consecutive images at 4–5 mm (more on thinner slices)
normal_values.extrusion_beyond_tibial_margin: ≤3 mm at the medial tibial spine; asymptomatic adults average about 1–2 mm

variants_pitfalls: Absent bow tie is non-specific (28% of normal menisci in one series; also small menisci, degeneration, prior meniscectomy); base a bucket-handle call on the displaced fragment, seen in 94% of bucket-handle tears.
Extrusion over 3 mm: root tear in 42% vs 3% at 3 mm or less, so check the posterior root. Measure at the medial tibial spine; the most-extruded slice overestimates it.
A low-signal nodule beside or below the medial plateau, deep to the MCL, with a truncated body is a displaced flap, not extrusion or an osteophyte; easily missed.
Flounce (an S-shaped free edge, 0.2–11%) usually flattens in full extension; accept it only after excluding a tear, as most in one series sat in torn menisci.
